subject: Encryption attestations + temporary access snapshot request
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@logistream.io>
Cc: LogiStream Ops <ops@logistream.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Encryption attestations + temporary access snapshot request

Hi Marta / LogiStream team,

We're preparing an updated subprocessor inventory for a subset of EU-regulated customers and need two items to complete our intake: 1) a vendor-side encryption attestation PDF (covering at-rest and in-transit controls, key management, and whether customer-managed keys are supported), and 2) a timebound snapshot of any personnel or third-party contractors who had temporary admin or elevated access to LogiStream systems in the last 12 months (names + roles + access window).

Specifically, our security reviewers are asking for:
- Scope of encryption (service, backups, logs) and KMS provider(s) used
- Any HSM/KMS integration details (e.g., AWS KMS vs. on-prem HSM)
- Proof/cert that backups are encrypted and chase frequency of backups
- A CSV snapshot listing subprocessor name, country, data scope, and whether access is persistent vs. temporary; for temporary entries please include start/end dates and approver.

If LogiStream already has a standard encryption attestation doc, that will do fine. We need the snapshot for our DPA amendment workflow and to feed into our transfer-impact assessment. Can you send the attestation and the CSV by end of day Monday (2026-09-21) US Pacific? If there are any export control or residency caveats we should be aware of, flag them in the same email.

Thanks,
Irene

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Marta Ruiz <marta@logistream.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Encryption attestations + temporary access snapshot request

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the clear list — attaching our encryption attestation PDF and a generated subprocessor snapshot CSV. High level notes inline:

- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for service and backups. We use AWS KMS for service keys; customer-managed keys are supported for dedicated accounts via CMKs.
- HSM: We do not run our own HSMs; KMS only.
- Backups: nightly encrypted backups retained 90 days; incremental snapshots every 6 hours.
- Subprocessor CSV: includes third-party partners and temporary contractors who had admin/API elevated access in the last 12 months. Rows flagged as TEMP have start/end columns populated.

Attachments: logistream_encryption_attestation_2026-08.pdf; subprocessor_snapshot_20260918.csv

Two caveats: 1) for some subcontractors in LATAM we list only company names (per contract) rather than individual names; 2) the CSV includes a small list of short-term consultants that had jump-bridge access for a 2-3 week window — we marked those as TEMP with approver notes.

If you need a signed version please confirm and we can route to our legal.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Ops
LogiStream
Attachment: logistream_encryption_attestation_2026-08.pdf (PDF)
Attachment: subprocessor_snapshot_20260918.csv (CSV)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@logistream.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption attestations + temporary access snapshot request

Thanks Marta — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our side after a quick review:

1) For the LATAM subcontractors where you redacted individual names, can you provide company-level SOC2/ISO attestations or point us to their compliance page? Our legal team needs evidence of organizational controls if individual-level data isn't shareable.

2) For the TEMP consultant rows: can you confirm whether those individuals had access to production customer data or only to observability/diagnostics environments? We need to classify the access level for our DPA.

3) Lastly, can you produce a simple one-page data flow diagram (PNG or PDF) that shows where customer content flows through LogiStream (ingest -> staging -> processing -> logs/backups) and which subprocessors handle each stage? That helps our transfer-impact assessment team map cross-border flows.

Looping in Kimberly (Legal) and Ben (Infosec) to triage any contractual or technical gaps. If a signed attestation is required we'll coordinate with Legal, but please indicate lead time for signature.

Target timeline from our end: need answers to Q1/Q2 and a draft flow diagram by EOD Tuesday (2026-09-21) Pacific to stay on schedule for a DPA amendment.

Thanks,
Irene

--
Kimberly Park (cc'd) will confirm any contract asks; Ben will confirm whether TEMP access to non-prod is acceptable with our compensating controls.
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption attestations + temporary access snapshot request

Irene / Kimberly,

Reviewed the CSV and attestation. Quick summary:
- Attestation looks complete for our baseline. Confirmed AES-256 and AWS KMS support for CMKs.
- TEMP consultants: 3 individuals had temporary elevated access; per Marta's note two were limited to diagnostics/non-prod and one had limited production read-only access for troubleshooting (no write). For the read-only access, we want the session logs (dates/times) exported as evidence; request to LogiStream below.
- LATAM subcontractors: if they can provide org-level SOC2/ISO or evidence of equivalent technical controls we can accept company-level attestations. If not available, we'll escalate to Legal for an exceptions flow.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly please confirm whether a signed attestation is required for the DPA amendment (I suspect yes).
2) Irene, I'll draft the evidence email to LogiStream requesting session logs for the one read-only production access.

Ben

Senior Security Engineer
